title: ENGLISH GRAMMAR
subtitle: Transformation and Synthesis of Sentences
description: Comprehensive practice test set containing 50 high-yield objective MCQs on Transformation and Synthesis of Sentences.

questions.q: He is too weak to walk without support. -> Complex sentence:
o: He is so weak that he cannot walk without support.
He is very weak and cannot walk without support.
He being weak cannot walk without support.
He is too weak so that he cannot walk.

questions.q: Besides being intelligent, she is diligent. -> Compound sentence:
o: She is not only intelligent but also diligent.
She is intelligent as well as diligent.
Being intelligent she is diligent too.
She is intelligent so she is diligent.

questions.q: Owing to his illness, he could not attend office. -> Complex sentence:
o: As he was ill, he could not attend office.
He was ill and so he could not attend office.
He being ill could not attend office.
He was ill so he did not attend office.

questions.q: Seeing a snake, the boy fled away in fear. -> Complex sentence:
o: When the boy saw a snake, he fled away in fear.
The boy saw a snake and he fled away in fear.
The boy fled away because he saw a snake.
Seeing a snake made the boy flee in fear.

questions.q: Only a brave man can face such a crisis. -> Negative sentence:
o: None but a brave man can face such a crisis.
No brave man can face such a crisis easily.
Every man cannot face such a crisis bravely.
A brave man never fails to face such a crisis.

questions.q: As soon as the sun rose, the fog disappeared. -> Negative sentence:
o: No sooner did the sun rise than the fog disappeared.
The sun rose and immediately the fog disappeared.
Scarcely had the sun risen when fog disappeared.
The fog did not disappear until sun rose up.

questions.q: Every mother loves her child deeply. -> Negative sentence:
o: There is no mother who does not love her child.
No mother loves her child deeply and truly.
A mother never hates her own child.
Mother does not love her child at all times.

questions.q: Who can touch pitch and not be defiled? -> Assertive sentence:
o: No one can touch pitch without being defiled.
Everyone can touch pitch without being defiled.
Anyone can touch pitch and be defiled.
Touch pitch and you will be defiled.

questions.q: Can a leopard change its spots? -> Assertive sentence:
o: A leopard cannot change its spots.
A leopard can easily change its spots.
Every leopard can change its spots.
No leopard wants to change its spots.

questions.q: What a beautiful landscape this is! -> Assertive sentence:
o: This is a very beautiful landscape.
Is this a very beautiful landscape?
How beautiful this landscape really is!
This landscape is not beautiful at all.

questions.q: How sweet the moonlight sleeps upon this bank! -> Assertive sentence:
o: The moonlight sleeps very sweetly upon this bank.
Does the moonlight sleep sweetly upon this bank?
The moonlight does not sleep upon this bank.
How sweetly does the moonlight sleep here!

questions.q: Mumbai is the richest city in India. -> Comparative degree:
o: Mumbai is richer than any other city in India.
No other city in India is as rich as Mumbai.
Mumbai is richer than many other cities in India.
Very few cities in India are as rich as Mumbai.

questions.q: Iron is the most useful of all metals. -> Positive degree:
o: No other metal is as useful as iron.
Iron is more useful than any other metal.
Very few metals are as useful as iron.
Iron is useful compared to other metals.

questions.q: He is as strong as his elder brother Rahul. -> Comparative degree:
o: His elder brother Rahul is not stronger than he.
His elder brother Rahul is stronger than he.
He is stronger than his elder brother Rahul.
Rahul is as strong as he is in reality.

questions.q: Shakespeare was greater than any other English poet. -> Superlative degree:
o: Shakespeare was the greatest poet of all time.
Shakespeare was the greatest of all English poets.
No other English poet was as great as Shakespeare.
Shakespeare was one of the greatest English poets.

questions.q: Very few Indian cities are as large as Kolkata. -> Comparative degree:
o: Kolkata is larger than any other Indian city.
Kolkata is larger than most other Indian cities.
Kolkata is the largest city in all of India.
No other Indian city is larger than Kolkata.

questions.q: Combine: The sun set. The night fell. -> Simple sentence using Nominative Absolute:
o: When the sun set, the night fell quietly.
The sun having set, the night fell.
The sun set and the night fell quickly.
As the sun set, the night fell down.

questions.q: Combine: He heard the bad news. He fainted. -> Simple sentence using Participle:
o: He heard the bad news and he fainted.
On hearing the bad news, he fainted.
When he heard bad news, he fainted.
Because he heard news, he fainted.

questions.q: Combine: He worked hard. He wanted to win prize. -> Simple sentence using Infinitive:
o: He worked hard and won the prize.
He worked hard to win the prize.
Working hard made him win the prize.
He worked hard so that he wins.

questions.q: Combine: This is Tagore. He wrote the Gitanjali. -> Simple sentence using Noun in Apposition:
o: Tagore wrote the famous book Gitanjali.
Tagore, the author of Gitanjali, is this man.
Tagore who wrote Gitanjali is famous.
This is Tagore and he wrote Gitanjali.

questions.q: Combine: He was honest. He was praised. -> Simple sentence using Preposition with Noun:
o: He was praised because he was honest.
In spite of his honesty, he was praised.
He was praised for his honesty.
Being praised, he was very honest.

questions.q: Combine: The rain stopped. We resumed journey. -> Simple sentence using Nominative Absolute:
o: When rain stopped, we resumed journey.
The rain stopped and we resumed journey.
The rain having stopped, we resumed our journey.
After rain stopped, we resumed journey.

questions.q: Combine: He ran fast. He missed the morning train. -> Compound sentence using Adversative:
o: Though he ran fast, he missed train.
Running fast, he missed morning train.
He ran fast, yet he missed the train.
He ran fast because he missed train.

questions.q: Combine: Work hard. You will fail the test. -> Compound sentence using Alternative:
o: If you do not work hard, you fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
Work hard, or you will fail the test.
Working hard prevents failing test.

questions.q: Combine: He was ill. He could not come. -> Compound sentence using Illative:
o: As he was ill, he could not come.
He being ill could not come here.
He was ill, therefore he could not come.
Because of illness he did not come.

questions.q: Combine: He is rich. He is unhappy. -> Complex sentence using Concessive clause:
o: He is rich, yet he is unhappy.
He is rich but he is unhappy.
Although he is rich, he is unhappy.
In spite of wealth he is unhappy.

questions.q: Combine: Tell me the truth. You will be punished. -> Complex sentence using Condition:
o: Tell truth or you will be punished.
Tell truth, otherwise you get punished.
Unless you tell the truth, you will be punished.
Tell truth so you are not punished.

questions.q: Combine: He reached school. The bell rang. -> Complex sentence using Time clause:
o: He reached school and bell rang.
On reaching school the bell rang.
As soon as he reached school, the bell rang.
Reaching school made bell ring.

questions.q: Combine: This is the house. I was born here. -> Complex sentence using Relative Adverb:
o: I was born in this very house.
This is house and I was born here.
This is the house where I was born.
Being born here, this is my house.

questions.q: Combine: The man died. He was very honest. -> Complex sentence using Relative Pronoun:
o: An honest man died yesterday.
The honest man died in hospital.
The man who was very honest died.
The man died because he was honest.

questions.q: He confessed his crime before court. -> Complex sentence with Noun Clause:
o: He confessed about his crime.
He confessed his own crime.
He confessed that he had committed the crime.
His crime was confessed by him.

questions.q: I know his birthplace. -> Complex sentence with Noun Clause:
o: I know the place of his birth.
I know where he was born.
I know where he was born.
I know his exact birth place.

questions.q: He promised to help me in need. -> Complex sentence with Noun Clause:
o: He promised helping me in need.
He promised his help to me.
He promised that he would help me in need.
He promised help when I needed.

questions.q: On seeing police, thief ran away. -> Compound sentence:
o: When thief saw police, he ran.
The thief saw police and ran away.
The thief saw police and ran away immediately.
As thief saw police, he ran.

questions.q: In spite of hard work, he failed. -> Compound sentence:
o: Although he worked hard, he failed.
Though working hard, he failed.
He worked hard, but he failed.
He failed because he worked hard.

questions.q: To avoid fine, you must pay bill. -> Compound sentence:
o: If you avoid fine, pay bill.
You must pay bill to avoid fine.
You must pay the bill, or you will be fined.
Unless you pay bill, you get fined.

questions.q: He is too old to run fast. -> Remove 'too':
o: He is very old to run fast.
He is extremely old to run fast.
He is so old that he can run fast.
He is so old that he cannot run fast.

questions.q: The news is too good to be true. -> Remove 'too':
o: The news is very good to be true.
The news is extremely good to be true.
The news is so good that it is true.
The news is so good that it cannot be true.

questions.q: She was too tired to walk further. -> Remove 'too':
o: She was very tired to walk further.
She was extremely tired to walk.
She was so tired that she could walk.
She was so tired that she could not walk further.

questions.q: Where there is smoke, there is fire. -> Affirmative sentence:
o: Smoke and fire are always together.
Fire causes smoke to rise up.
There is smoke whenever fire burns.
There is no smoke without fire.

questions.q: As soon as I entered, he left. -> Inverted negative form:
o: As I entered, he left room.
Hardly I entered when he left.
Scarcely I entered than he left.
No sooner did I enter than he left.

questions.q: Everyone will admit his honesty. -> Negative sentence without changing sense:
o: Everyone will not deny his honesty.
No one will admit his honesty.
No one will doubt his honesty.
No one will deny his honesty.

questions.q: He is a man of great courage. -> Complex sentence using Adjective Clause:
o: He is a very courageous man.
He has great courage in him.
He is courageous and strong.
He is a man who possesses great courage.

questions.q: I bought a house belonging to Rahul. -> Complex sentence using Adjective Clause:
o: I bought Rahul's own house.
I bought a house of Rahul.
The house bought belonged to Rahul.
I bought a house which belonged to Rahul.

questions.q: He came here at sunset. -> Complex sentence using Adverb Clause:
o: He came here during sunset time.
He came here when sun was setting.
He came here at the time of sunset.
He came here when the sun set.

questions.q: He acted according to instructions. -> Complex sentence using Adverb Clause:
o: He acted as per given instructions.
He acted following instructions.
He acted upon given instructions.
He acted as he was instructed.

questions.q: Owing to storm, flight was cancelled. -> Complex sentence using Adverb Clause:
o: Storm caused flight cancellation.
The flight was cancelled by storm.
Flight was cancelled owing to storm.
As there was a storm, the flight was cancelled.

questions.q: He worked hard to win prize. -> Complex sentence using Adverb Clause:
o: He worked hard for winning prize.
He worked hard and won prize.
Working hard he won the prize.
He worked hard so that he might win prize.

questions.q: In spite of poverty, he is honest. -> Complex sentence using Adverb Clause:
o: He is poor but he is honest.
He is honest despite poverty.
Being poor he is honest.
Although he is poor, he is honest.

questions.q: Do or die. -> Complex sentence using Conditional Clause:
o: Do and die immediately.
If you do, you die.
Unless you do, you do not die.
If you do not do, you will die.
